abstract: Across vertebrate species, it has long been known that germline mutation rates per year are inversely proportional to reproductive ages. A similar pattern was recently reported in mammals for mutations in colonic epithelium, leading to speculation that this inter-species scaling may apply to many cell types. We tested whether a similar relationship holds in postmitotic cells, by estimating point mutation rates in mouse cortical neurons from PacBio HiFi circular consensus sequencing data. Our analysis revealed a significant effect of age on the number of point mutations, of 25.9 mutations per diploid genome per year (95% CI: [17.7, 34.1]). This rate is comparable to the one reported for human neurons, indicating that somatic rates need not scale with lifespan. Our findings further demonstrate that a readily available sequencing method can be used to reliably identify somatic mutations at single-cell resolution.
